name: manual_7c81ff
claim: A budget/rate guard whose check-then-act calls (can_spend/record_spend) straddle a real await point has a genuine TOCTOU race under concurrency -- fix with an atomic reserve()/commit()/rollback() pattern holding the reservation (counting other in-flight reservations, not just settled state) before the await, not just adding a lock around the two separate calls

decisions.notes: orchestrator/fastapi_app.py's /orchestrate endpoint called cost_guard.can_spend() then, after an await _resolve_candidates(...), cost_guard.record_spend() -- two concurrent requests could both pass can_spend() before either recorded spend, jointly overspending the daily budget. This is the same TOCTOU class Tier5BudgetLedger's reserve/settle pattern already solved for a different subsystem, but the fix hadn't been generalized to CostGuard. Added CostGuard.reserve()/commit()/rollback() with an asyncio.Lock and an in-flight _reserved dict checked alongside settled daily_spend -- reserve() must count OTHER pending reservations, not just what's already on disk, or two reserves can both pass concurrently. Verified with a real asyncio.gather() concurrency test (5 tasks, exactly 1 can fit under budget, exactly 1 must win) -- sequential calls alone don't prove a lock actually serializes under real concurrency.
